paragraphs: Granite Construction Company was incorporated in 1922. In 1990, Granite Construction Incorporated was formed as the holding company for Granite Construction Company and its wholly-owned and consolidated subsidiaries and was incorporated in Delaware. Unless otherwise indicated, the terms "we," "us," "our," "Company" and "Granite" refer to Granite Construction Incorporated and its wholly-owned and consolidated subsidiaries.

We deliver infrastructure solutions for public and private clients primarily in the United States. We are one of the largest diversified, vertically integrated civil contractors and construction materials producers in the United States. Within the public sector, we primarily concentrate on infrastructure projects, including the construction of streets, roads, highways, mass transit facilities, airport infrastructure, bridges, dams, power-related facilities, utilities, tunnels, water well drilling and other infrastructure-related projects. Within the private sector, we perform various services such as site preparation, mining services and infrastructure services for commercial and industrial sites, railways, residential development, energy development, as well as provide construction management professional services. We own and lease aggregate reserves, and we own processing plants that are vertically integrated into our construction operations. We also produce construction materials for sale to third parties.

We have vertically integrated operations across Alaska, Arizona, California, Kentucky, Louisiana, Mississippi, Nevada, Oregon, Tennessee, Utah and Washington in addition to regional civil construction home markets in the Midwest, Florida and Texas. Our Construction segment also operates national businesses within the Tunnel division and the Federal division, which performs civil construction across the continental United States and Guam, the Industrial & Energy division, which primarily focuses on commercial solar construction projects, and the Layne division, which performs water well drilling, rehabilitation services and mineral exploration services.

Our reportable segments are the same as our operating segments and correspond with how our chief operating decision maker, or decision-making group (our "CODM"), regularly reviews financial information to allocate resources and assess performance. We previously identified our CODM as our Chief Executive Officer ("CEO") and our Chief Operating Officer ("COO"). Following our COO's retirement on July 4, 2025, our CEO assumed sole responsibility as the CODM. Our reportable segments are: Construction and Materials. The Construction segment focuses on construction and rehabilitation of roads, pavement preservation, bridges, rail lines, airports, marine ports, dams, reservoirs, aqueducts, infrastructure and site development for use by the general public and water-related construction for municipal agencies, commercial water suppliers, industrial facilities and energy companies. It also provides construction of various complex projects including infrastructure and site development, mining, public safety, tunnel, solar, battery storage and other power-related projects. The Materials segment focuses on production and delivery of aggregates, asphalt concrete, liquid asphalt and recycled materials for internal use in our construction projects and for sale to third parties. See Note 21 of "Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements" for additional information about our reportable segments.

Customers in our Construction segment are predominantly in the public sector and include certain federal agencies, state departments of transportation, local transit authorities, county and city public works departments, school districts and developers, utilities and private owners of industrial, commercial and residential sites. Customers of our Materials segment include internal usage by our own construction projects, as well as third-party customers. Our third-party Materials segment customers include, but are not limited to, contractors, landscapers, manufacturers of products requiring aggregate materials, retailers, homeowners, farmers and brokers. The majority of our customers are located in the United States.

During the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, our largest volume customer, including both prime and subcontractor arrangements, was the California Department of Transportation ("Caltrans"). Revenue recognized from contracts with Caltrans during the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023 represented $446.6 million (10.1% of total revenue), $567.6 million (14.2% of total revenue) and $458.2 million (13.1% of total revenue), respectively, which was primarily in the Construction segment. Other than Caltrans, none of our customers, including both prime and subcontractor arrangements, had revenue that individually exceeded 10% of total revenue during the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 or 2023.

As America's Infrastructure Company(TM), Granite satisfies society's needs for mobility, power, water and other essential services that sustain living conditions and improve quality of life. Across our footprint of regional offices, we provide

horizontal civil infrastructure construction services and construction materials products to a diverse base of public, industrial and commercial clients. These clients benefit from our home market strategy which includes local relationships, market intelligence and the resources and expertise of one of the oldest and most respected U.S. contractors and materials producers.

Local market knowledge, relationships, and project management expertise, supported by the financial strength of a publicly traded company with a strong balance sheet, provide a sustainable competitive advantage. By diversifying our revenue channels across geographies and clients, and by taking measured risks within our construction capabilities, we simultaneously grow our business and mitigate risk. Supported by proven operating processes, functional support systems and financial governance processes, our growing network of regional businesses focus on local market conditions, client relationships, employee development, workforce capabilities and investment opportunities to drive growth and efficiency within their home markets.
Additionally, the following continue to be key objectives in our strategic plan:

Selective Bidding: We focus our resources on bidding jobs that meet our bidding criteria, which include analyzing the risk of a potential job relative to: (1) available personnel to estimate and prepare the proposal as well as to effectively manage and build the project; (2) project procurement methodology; (3) the competitive environment; (4) our experience with the type of work and the owner; (5) local resources and partnerships; (6) equipment resources; and (7) the size, duration, complexity and expected profitability of the job.

Risk-Balanced Growth: We intend to grow our business by strategically adding to our client base within our current geographic markets and expanding into new geographic areas both organically and through acquisitions. Growth opportunities are evaluated relative to their incremental impact to the execution risk and profitability profile of our operating portfolio.

Vertical Integration: We own and lease aggregate reserves and own processing plants that are vertically integrated into our construction operations. By ensuring the availability of these resources through strategic expansion and providing quality products, we believe we have a competitive advantage in many of our markets, as well as a source of revenue and earnings from the sale of construction materials to third parties. We also look for additional vertical integration opportunities that complement our existing construction and materials businesses. In 2025, we continued to strengthen and expand our vertically integrated home markets with acquisitions of Slats Lucas, LLC and Warren Paving, Inc. (collectively, "Warren Paving"), a vertically-integrated asphalt contractor and aggregate producer with operations along the Gulf Coast and Mississippi River; Papich Construction Company, Inc. ("Papich Construction"), a provider of construction services and materials in California's Central Coast and Central Valley regions; and Cinderlite Trucking Corporation ("Cinderlite"), a construction materials, landscape supply and transportation company in Carson City, Nevada.

Diversification: To mitigate the risks inherent in the construction business as the result of general economic factors, we pursue projects: (1) in both the public and private sectors; (2) in diverse end markets such as federal, rail, power and water; (3) for a wide range of clients from the federal government to small municipalities and from large corporations to small private customers; (4) in diverse geographic markets; (5) with procurement methods that include construction management/general contractor ("CM/GC"), construction management at-risk ("CMAR"), progressive design-build, bid-build and design-build; (6) that are executed according to a fixed price, time and materials, cost reimbursable and fixed unit price; and (7) of various size, duration and complexity.

Set forth below and elsewhere in this report and in other documents we file with the SEC are various risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from the results contemplated by the forward-looking statements contained in this report or otherwise adversely affect our business.

•Unfavorable economic conditions may have an adverse impact on our business. Volatility in the global financial system, deterioration in general economic activity, inflation, rising or high interest rates, tariffs, supply chain issues, wars or other geopolitical tensions, other political, social or economic uncertainties, and fiscal, monetary and other policies that federal, state and local governments may enact, including infrastructure spending or deficit reduction measures, may have an adverse impact on our business, financial position, results of operations, cash flows and liquidity. In particular, low tax revenues, budget deficits, financing constraints, including timing of long-term federal, state and local funding releases, and competing priorities could negatively impact the ability of government agencies to fund existing or new infrastructure projects in the public sector. These factors could have a material adverse effect on the financial market and economic conditions in the United States as well as throughout the world, which may limit our ability and the ability of our customers to obtain financing and/or could impair our ability to execute our strategy.

•We work in a highly competitive marketplace. We have multiple competitors in all the areas in which we work, and some of our competitors are larger than we are and may have greater resources than we do. Government funding for public works projects is limited, contributing to competition. An increase in competition may result in a decrease in new awards, a decrease in profit margins, or both. In addition, should downturns in residential and commercial construction activity occur, the competition for available public sector work would intensify, which could impact our revenue, CAP and profit margins.

•Fixed price and fixed unit price contracts subject us to the risk of increased project cost. As more fully described in "Contract Provisions and Subcontracting" under "Item 1. Business," the profitability of our fixed price and fixed unit price contracts can be adversely affected by a number of factors, including, among others, inflation, tariffs, inefficiency and incorrect estimates or assumptions, that can cause our actual costs to materially exceed the costs estimated at the time of our original bid. This could result in reduced profits or a loss for that project and there could be a material adverse impact to our business, results of operations and financial condition.

•We derive a substantial amount of our revenue from federal, state and local government agencies, and any disruption in government funding or in our relationship with those agencies could adversely affect our business. For the year ended December 31, 2025, approximately 70% of our construction revenue was funded by federal, state and local government agencies and authorities. A significant amount of this revenue is derived under multi-year contracts, many of which are appropriated on an annual basis. As a result, at the beginning of a project, the related contract may be only partially funded, and additional funding is normally committed only as appropriations are made in each subsequent year. The success and further development of our business depends, in large part, upon the continued funding of these government programs, and upon our ability to obtain contracts and perform well under these programs. A significant reduction in government spending, the absence of a bipartisan agreement on the federal government budget, a partial or full federal government shutdown or a change in budgetary priorities could reduce demand for our services, cancel or delay projects and have a material adverse effect on our business, results of operations and financial condition.

There are several additional factors that could cause government agencies or authorities to delay or cancel programs, to reduce their orders under existing contracts, to exercise their rights to terminate contracts or not to exercise contract options for renewals or extensions. The five primary economic drivers of our business are (i) the overall health of the U.S. economy including access to resources (labor, supplies and subcontractors); (ii) federal, state and local public funding levels; (iii) population growth resulting in public and private development; (iv) the need to build, replace or repair aging infrastructure; and (v) the pricing of certain commodity related products. A stagnant or declining economy will generally result in reduced demand for construction and construction materials in the private sector. This reduced demand increases competition for private sector projects and will ultimately also increase competition in the public sector as companies migrate from bidding on scarce private sector work to projects in the public sector. In addition, a stagnant or declining economy tends to produce less tax revenue for public agencies, thereby decreasing a source of funds available for spending on public infrastructure improvements. Some funding sources that have been specifically earmarked for infrastructure spending, such as diesel and gasoline taxes, are not as directly affected by a stagnant or declining economy, unless actual consumption is reduced or gasoline sales tax revenues decline consistent with fuel prices. However, even these can be temporarily at risk as federal, state and local governments take actions to balance their budgets. Conversely, increased levels of public funding as well as an expanding or robust economy will generally increase demand for our services and products and provide opportunities for revenue growth and margin improvement.

The financial statements included in "Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data" have been prepared in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America ("U.S. GAAP"). The preparation of these financial statements requires management to make estimates that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities, revenue and expenses, and related disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities. Our estimates and related judgments and assumptions are continually evaluated based on available information and experiences; however, actual amounts could differ from those estimates.

Our revenue is primarily derived from construction contracts that can span several quarters or years in our Construction segment and from sales of construction related materials in our Materials segment. We recognize revenue in accordance with ASC Topic 606, Revenue from Contracts with Customers, and subsequently issued additional related ASUs. The accuracy of our revenue and profit recognition in a given period depends on the accuracy of our estimates of the forecasted revenue and cost to complete each project. Cost estimates for all of our significant projects use a detailed "bottom up" approach. There are a number of factors that can contribute to changes in estimates of contract cost and profitability. The most significant of these include:
•changes in costs of labor and/or materials; •subcontractor costs, availability and/or performance issues;
•extended overhead and other costs due to owner, weather and other delays; •changes in productivity expectations;

paragraphs: Granite Construction Company 於 1922 年設立。1990 年，Granite Construction Incorporated 成立為 Granite Construction Company 及其全部擁有並合併子公司之控股公司，並在特拉華州設立。除非另有說明，本文中 "we"、"us"、"our"、"Company" 及 "Granite" 皆指 Granite Construction Incorporated 及其全部擁有並合併子公司。

我們為公部門與私部門客戶提供基礎設施解決方案，主要服務美國市場。我們是美國規模最大的多元化、垂直整合之土木承包商與建設材料生產商之一。在公部門方面，我們主要專注於基礎設施工程，包括街道、道路、高速公路、大眾運輸設施、機場基礎設施、橋樑、水壩、電力相關設施、公用設施、隧道、水井鑽探及其他基礎設施相關工程。在私部門方面，我們提供各種服務，如商業與工業場地之場地準備、採礦服務及基礎設施服務，以及鐵路、住宅開發、能源開發，並提供建設管理專業服務。我們擁有並租賃礦產儲備，並擁有與建設作業垂直整合之加工廠。我們亦生產建設材料供第三方銷售。
我們在阿拉斯加、亞利桑那、加州、肯塔基、路易斯安那、密西西比、內華達、俄勒岡、田納西、猶他及華盛頓州擁有垂直整合之營運，並在中西部、佛羅裏達及德州擁有區域性土木建設主要市場。我們的建設分部亦在隧道部門及聯邦部門內運作全國性業務，這些部門執行美國本土及關島之土木建設，工業與能源部門主要專注於商業太陽能建設項目，而Layne部門則執行水井鑽探、復原服務及礦物探勘服務。

我們的應報告分部與營運分部相同，並與我們的首席營運決策者（或決策羣組，我們稱為 "CODM"）如何定期審閱財務資訊以分配資源及評估績效方式一致。我們先前將 CODM 識別為我們的首席執行長（"CEO"）及首席營運長（"COO"）。在 2025 年 7 月 4 日 COO 退休後，CEO 接手獨自擔任 CODM。我們的應報告分部為建設與材料。建設分部專注於道路建設與復原、路面維護、橋樑、鐵路、機場、海港、水壩、水庫、水道、基礎設施及場地開發，供一般大眾使用，以及為地方政府機構、商業用水供應商、工業設施及能源公司執行水相關建設。該分部亦提供各種複雜工程之建設，包括基礎設施及場地開發、採礦、公共安全、隧道、太陽能、電池儲能及其他電力相關工程。材料分部專注於生產與配送礦產、瀝青混凝土、液態瀝青及回收材料，供我們建設項目內部使用及銷售給第三方。請參閱 "合併財務報表附註" 中的附註 21，以取得更多關於我們應報告分部之資訊。
我們建設分部之客戶主要來自公部門，包括某些聯邦機構、州交通部、地方捷運機構、縣市公共工程處、學校區、開發商、電力公司及私人擁有之工業、商業及住宅場地。我們材料分部之客戶包括我們建設項目之內部使用，以及第三方客戶。我們第三方材料分部客戶包括但不限於承包商、園藝師、需要礦產材料之產品製造商、零售商、住宅所有者、農民及經紀人。我們絕大多數客戶位於美國。

在截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日、2024 年 12 月 31 日及 2023 年 12 月 31 日之會計年度中，我們最大體積客戶（包括總承包與分包安排）為加州交通部（"Caltrans"）。與 Caltrans 籤訂合約所認列之收入，在截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日、2024 年 12 月 31 日及 2023 年 12 月 31 日之會計年度中分別為 4.466 億美元（佔總營業收入 10.1%）、5.676 億美元（佔總營業收入 14.2%）及 4.582 億美元（佔總營業收入 13.1%），主要為建設分部。除 Caltrans 之外，我們的客戶（包括總承包與分包安排）在截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日、2024 年 12 月 31 日或 2023 年 12 月 31 日之會計年度中，無任何客戶之收入 individually 超過總營業收入 10%。
作為美國基礎設施公司（"America's Infrastructure Company(TM)"），Granite 滿足社會對移動性、電力、水及其他維繫生活條件並提升生活品質之基本服務需求。在我們的區域辦公室網路中，我們提供
水平式土木基礎設施建設服務及建設材料產品給多樣化的公部門、工業及商業客戶。這些客戶受益於我們的本地市場策略，包括本地關係、市場資訊以及美國最悠久且最受尊敬的建設承包商與材料生產商之一的資源與專業知識。
在地市場知識、人際關係與專案管理專業，搭配公開上市公司的財務實力與強固資產負債結構，提供可持續的競爭優勢。透過跨地理區域與客戶的收入渠道多元化，並在建設能力範圍內審慎評估風險，我們同時拓展業務並降低風險。透過已驗證的運營流程、功能支援系統與財務治理程序，我們日益擴張的區域性企業網路專注於在地市場條件、客戶關係、員工發展、人力資源能力與投資機會，以推動其本市場的成長與效率。
此外，以下項目仍為我們戰略計畫中的關鍵目標：
選擇性投標：我們將資源集中於符合投標標準的項目，這些標準包括分析潛在項目風險，相對於：(1) 可用人力以評估與準備提案，以及有效管理與執行專案；(2) 專案採購方法；(3) 競爭環境；(4) 我們對該類工作與業主的經驗；(5) 地區資源與合作夥伴；(6) 裝備資源；以及(7) 專案的規模、持續時間、複雜度與預期獲利性。
風險平衡成長：我們透過在現有地理市場內擴大客戶羣，並透過內生與收購方式拓展至新地理區域，來有意識地成長業務。成長機會會根據其對運營組合執行風險與獲利性質的增量影響進行評估。

垂直整合：我們擁有並租賃總計儲備，並擁有處理廠，這些資源與我們的建設運營垂直整合。透過戰略擴張確保這些資源的可用性，並提供高品質產品，我們相信在許多市場中擁有競爭優勢，同時也從向第三方銷售建設材料中獲得收入與獲利。我們也尋找與現有建設與材料業務相輔相成的垂直整合機會。2025年，我們持續強化並擴張我們的垂直整合住宅市場，收購了Slats Lucas, LLC與Warren Paving, Inc.（合稱"Warren Paving"），一家垂直整合的瀝青承包商與礦物質生產商，業務範圍沿墨西哥灣沿岸與密西西比河；Papich Construction Company, Inc.（"Papich Construction"），一家在加利福尼亞州中央海岸與中央谷地地區提供建設服務與材料的公司；以及Cinderlite Trucking Corporation（"Cinderlite"），一家位於內華達州卡森城的建設材料、景觀供應與運輸公司。

多元化：為降低建設業務因總體經濟因素而產生的風險，我們追求：(1) 公部門與私部門的項目；(2) 多元化的終端市場，如聯邦政府、鐵路、電力與水；(3) 各種客戶，從聯邦政府到小型市鎮，從大型企業到小型私人客戶；(4) 多元化的地理市場；(5) 包括建設管理/總承包商（"CM/GC"）、建設管理風險承擔（"CMAR"）、漸進設計建造、招標建造與設計建造的採購方法；(6) 依據固定價格、時間與材料、成本賠償與固定單價執行的項目；以及(7) 各種規模、持續時間與複雜度的項目。

paragraphs: 我們提供基礎建設解決方案給公部門與私部門客戶，主要位於美國。我們是美國最大的多元化、垂直整合的民用工程承包商與建設材料生產商之一。在公部門方面，我們主要專注於基礎建設項目，包括街道、道路、高速公路、大眾運輸設施、機場基礎建設、橋樑、水壩、電力相關設施、公用設施、隧道、水井鑽探及其他基礎建設相關項目。在私部門方面，我們提供各種服務，例如商業與工業場地的場地準備、採礦服務與基礎建設服務、鐵路、住宅開發、能源開發，以及提供建設管理專業服務。我們擁有並出租礦物儲備，並擁有處理廠，這些處理廠與我們的建設運營垂直整合，我們也生產建設材料供第三方銷售。
我們在阿拉斯加、亞利桑那、加州、肯塔基、路易斯安那、密西西比、內華達、俄勒岡、田納西、猶他和華盛頓州擁有垂直整合的運營，並在中西部、佛羅裏達和德州擁有區域性的民用建設住宅市場。我們的建設部門也運營全國性的業務，包括隧道部門與聯邦部門，這些部門在美國大陸與關島進行民用建設，工業與能源部門主要專注於商業太陽能建設項目，以及Layne部門，該部門進行水井鑽探、復原服務與礦物探勘服務。

我們的應報告分部與我們的運營分部相同，並與我們的首席運營決策者（或決策小組）（我們的「CODM」）如何定期審閱財務資訊以分配資源並評估績效的方式一致。我們先前將CODM識別為我們的首席執行官（「CEO」）與首席運營官（「COO」）。在2025年7月4日COO退休後，CEO接任獨自擔任CODM。我們的應報告分部為：建設與材料。建設分部專注於道路建設與復原、路面維護、橋樑、鐵路、機場、海港、水壩、水庫、水道、基礎建設與場地開發，供公眾使用，以及為市府機關、商業用水供應商、工業設施與能源公司進行的水相關建設。它也提供各種複雜項目的建設，包括基礎建設與場地開發、採礦、公共安全、隧道、太陽能、電池儲能及其他電力相關項目。材料分部專注於生產與配送礦物、瀝青混凝土、液態瀝青與回收材料，供我們建設項目內部使用及銷售給第三方。請參閱「財務報表附註」第21項以取得更多關於我們應報告分部的資訊。

我們業務的五大主要經濟驅動因素為（i）美國經濟整體狀況，包括對資源（勞動力、供應與分包商）的可取得性；（ii）聯邦、州與地方政府的公共資金水平；（iii）人口成長導致公部門與私部門的開發；（iv）需要建設、更換或修復老舊基礎建設；（v）某些與商品相關產品的價格。經濟停滯或衰退通常會導致私部門對建設與建設材料需求減少。這種減少的需求會增加私部門項目之間的競爭，最終也會增加公部門的競爭，因為公司會從競標有限的私部門工作轉向公部門項目。此外，經濟停滯或衰退會導致公部門的稅收收入減少，從而減少可用於公共基礎建設改善的資金來源。一些特定用於基礎建設支出的資金來源，例如柴油與汽油稅，不會受到經濟停滯或衰退的直接影響，除非實際消費減少或汽油銷售稅收入因燃料價格而減少。然而，即使這些資金來源也可能因聯邦、州與地方政府採取行動平衡預算而暫時受到威脅。相反地，公共資金增加以及經濟擴張或強勁經濟通常會增加我們服務與產品的需求，並提供營收成長與毛利率改善的機會。
「項目8. 財務報表與補充資料」中包含的財務報表已根據美國通用會計準則（「U.S. GAAP」）編製。這些財務報表的編製需要管理層做出影響資產與負債、收入與費用以及相關或有資產與負債披露的估計。我們的估計與相關判斷與假設會根據現有資訊與經驗持續評估；然而，實際金額可能與這些估計不同。
以下為我們最關鍵的會計估計，涉及管理層判斷，並可能對我們的營運結果產生重大影響。

我們的收入主要來自建設合同，這些合同在建設分部中可能持續幾個季度或數年，在材料分部中則來自建設相關材料的銷售。我們根據ASC主題606「與客戶的合同收入」及後續發佈的相關ASUs進行收入確認。我們在特定期間內的收入與利潤確認準確性，取決於我們對每個項目預計收入與完成成本的估計準確性。我們所有重大項目的成本估計均採用詳細的「自下而上」方法。許多因素都可能導致合同成本與利潤率的估計變動。其中最重要的因素包括：
•勞動力與/或材料成本的變動；•分包商成本、可取得性與/或表現問題；
{'translated_text': '•擴充的間接費用及其他成本因業主、天氣及其他延誤所致；•生產力預期變動；'}
•設計建造專案中對原設計的變更;
•我們能否完全且及時回收肯定性聲請及追加契約成本的後補費用;
•設備及材料的取得與距離的變化；•原設計的複雜性；
•完成專案所需時間的長短；•專案所在地區勞工的取得與技能水準；
•現場條件與原標單所假設情況不同；•因範圍變更所產生的費用；以及
下列各項風險與不確定性說明，以及本報告其他部分與本公司向 SEC 提交之其他文件中所載之風險與不確定性，均可能導致本公司實際結果與本報告內所含之預測性陳述所預期之結果有重大差異，或對本公司業務產生不利影響。

• 不利之經濟條件可能對本公司業務產生不利影響。全球金融體系之波動、總體經濟活動之惡化、通貨膨脹、利率上漲或高利率、關稅、供應鏈問題、戰爭或其他地緣政治緊張情勢、其他政治、社會或經濟不確定性，以及聯邦、州與地方政府可能實施之財政、貨幣及其他政策，包括基礎建設支出或財赤減緩措施，均可能對本公司業務、財務狀況、營運結果、現金流及流動性產生不利影響。特別是，稅收收入偏低、財赤、融資限制，包括長期聯邦、州與地方資金釋放之時程，以及各項競爭優先事項，可能不利於政府機構執行現有或新基礎建設專案之財務能力。這些因素可能對美國以及全球之財務市場與總體經濟狀況產生重大不利影響，進而限制本公司與客戶取得融資之能力，或影響本公司執行戰略之能力。
• 本公司營運於高度競爭之市場。本公司在所有營運領域均有許多競爭對手，且部分競爭對手規模較本公司為大，且可能擁有較多資源。政府對公共工程之資金有限，進而加劇競爭。競爭增加可能導致新契約減少、利潤邊際下降，或二者兼有。此外，若住宅與商業建設活動出現衰退，則對公共部門工作之競爭將更加激烈，進而影響本公司之營收、CAP 及利潤邊際。
• 固定價格及固定單價契約使本公司面臨項目成本增加之風險。如「契約條款與分包」項目下所述，本公司固定價格及固定單價契約之獲利可能受多種因素影響，包括通貨膨脹、關稅、效率低下及錯誤之預估或假設，這些因素可能導致本公司實際成本大幅高於原始投標時之預估成本。這可能會導致該專案利潤減少或產生虧損，並對本公司業務、營運結果及財務狀況產生重大不利影響。

• 本公司大量營收來自聯邦、州與地方政府機構，任何政府資金中斷或與這些機構之關係受影響，均可能對本公司業務產生不利影響。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，約 70% 之建設營收來自聯邦、州與地方政府機構及權力機構。此營收中，大量來自於多年契約，其中許多契約係每年經撥款程序批准。因此，在專案開始時，相關契約可能僅部分資金到位，且額外資金通常僅在後續年度經撥款程序後才會承諾。本公司業務之成功與進一步發展，在很大程度上依賴於這些政府計畫之持續資金，以及本公司取得契約並在這些計畫下表現良好之能力。政府支出大幅減少、聯邦政府預算缺乏兩黨協議、聯邦政府部分或完全停擺，或預算優先順序改變，均可能減少對本公司服務之需求，取消或延遲專案，並對本公司業務、營運結果及財務狀況產生重大不利影響。
有數個其他因素可能導致政府機構或權力機構延遲或取消專案、減少現有契約下之訂單、行使終止契約之權利，或不執行契約選項以延續或延長契約。這些因素包括以下內容，可能對本公司業務、財務狀況及營運結果，或來自政府機構或權力機構之契約付款時程產生重大不利影響：
